name: Edil Medeiros
cooked:
I would like to see some work on evaluating transaction clustering based on network traffic, even though this line of research feels quite weak based on the papers I have seem so far.

Main starting point would be Transaction Clustering Using Network Traffic Analysis for Bitcoin and Derived Blockchains (I can provide full text). The paper has several limitations (small sample on testnet where the authors controlled a relevant part of the txs origins, data collected is not well described) but they claim using Tor would not help mitigate. That’s where the methodology might inspire something more realistic and useful because of related PRs and issues in Bitcoin Core:

  • Broadcast own transactions only via short-lived Tor or I2P connections by vasild · Pull Request #29415 · bitcoin/bitcoin · GitHub (merged)
  • net: send decoy transactions via private broadcast by andrewtoth · Pull Request #35252 · bitcoin/bitcoin · GitHub (closed)
  • https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36330 (draft)
  • wallet: Rethinking Transaction Rebroadcasting · Issue #36403 · bitcoin/bitcoin · GitHub (high level discussion)

Other references:

https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11172744

arXiv.org

Bitcoin over Tor isn't a good idea

Bitcoin is a decentralized P2P digital currency in which coins are generated by a distributed set of miners and transaction are broadcasted via a peer-to-peer network. While Bitcoin provides some level of anonymity (or rather pseudonymity) by...

Maybe Yuval (nothingmuch) or the guys on crocs muni may have more insights about this.
